Look for **gold/red foil** for extra festivity. - **DIY:** Use red paper (available at craft stores) + glue/stickers. Add a **gold seal (印章)** or calligraphy for a personal touch. - **Alternative:** Use **red envelopes with QR codes** (e.g., WeChat Pay/Alipay) for digital hongbao (if your cousins are tech-savvy). **B. Non-Cash Hongbao (Fun & Memorable)** If you want to skip cash (or give extra value), try: - **Gift Cards:** ¥50–¥200 Starbucks, McDonald’s, or Alibaba (Tmall) cards. Kids love these! - **Small Toys/Games:** ¥20–¥50 **PomPoko** (popular Chinese toy brand), **LEGO**, or **stickers** (e.g., Disney, Hello Kitty). - **Food Coupons:** Vouchers for their favorite snacks (e.g., "¥30 for a box of Mooncakes" or "¥50 for a meal at [local restaurant]"). - **Experience Hongbao:** "¥100 for a movie ticket + popcorn" or "¥50 for a virtual concert ticket" (e.g., Bilibili or Tencent Music). - **Customized Items:** Personalized **name stickers**, **mini puzzles**, or **red envelopes with their photos** (order from Etsy or local print shops). **C. Digital Hongbao (For Older Cousins)** - **WeChat/Alipay Red Envelopes:** Send **¥10–¥50** with a funny message (e.g., "For your future success! 🎉"). Add a **GIF** or **sticker** to make it special. - **Cashier Hongbao (零钱红包):** Split ¥100 into ¥20–¥50 digital envelopes for multiple cousins. --- ### **2. Last-Minute Tips** - **Buy in Bulk:** Supermarkets (e.g., Carrefour, H Mart) or **Taobao** often have red envelopes in packs. Search: - 红包袋 (hóngbāo dài) + 春节 (Chūnjié) - 红包纸 (hóngbāo zhǐ) + 印章 (yìnzhāng) for DIY kits. - **Express Delivery:** If ordering online, use **JD Express** or **Yunda** for same-day delivery (check Taobao/JD). - **Wrap It Nice:** Add a **red ribbon**, **gold washi tape**, or a **handwritten note** (e.g., "祝你新年快乐！" *Zhù nǐ xīnnián kuàilè!* = Happy New Year!). - **Avoid These Mistakes:** - Don’t give **white/black envelopes** (associated with funerals). - Skip **odd amounts** (e.g., ¥15) or ¥4 (bad luck). - Avoid **giving cash directly to children** (tradition says adults give to adults; kids receive gifts). --- ### **3. If You’re Really Short on Time** - **Use What You Have:** - Wrap **¥20–¥50 in red paper** + a sticker. - Give **a small toy + ¥10** (e.g., a keychain + cash). - **Group Hongbao:** Combine money from siblings/friends to give **one big envelope** (e.g., ¥200 total split among cousins). - **Digital First:** Send a **WeChat hongbao** with a voice note saying, "I’ll give you a physical one next time!" --- ### **4. Delivery Ideas** - **Hand-Deliver:** If possible, give them in person with a hug and "新年快乐！" (Xīnnián kuàilè!). - **Post It:** Use **China Post** (if they’re far) or **JD Courier** (fast and reliable). - **Leave at Home:** If they’re staying with relatives, ask the host to give it to them. --- ### **5. Even a **handmade envelope with ¥20 and a smile** will make them happy.
